title: Ensemble Dependence of the Critical Exponent at a Quantum Error Correction Threshold
abstract: In thermodynamics it is common to assume that the choice of ensemble (e.g., micro-canonical, canonical, or grand-canonical) should not affect the underlying physics in the thermodynamics limit. We show that this does not necessarily hold for critical exponents. Examining a simplified model of quantum error correction (single step encoding and decoding by a random unitary) and the behavior of both the fidelity and magic at the corresponding threshold, we find different exponents when using generic channels or supposedly equivalent quantum trajectories. Interestingly, the obtained exponents saturate a recently derived information theoretic bound by Feldman et al. (2026), which we extend from the grand-canonical to the canonical case, including intermediate ensembles which we define. Moreover, even the existence of the transition is shown to be ensemble-dependent.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that for quantum error correction thresholds, the critical exponents characterizing the phase transition are not universal but depend on the statistical ensemble used for averaging errors. By comparing canonical and grand-canonical ensembles, the authors find distinct exponents, challenging the common assumption of ensemble independence in critical phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the choice of thermodynamic ensemble (micro-canonical vs. canonical vs. grand-canonical) affects the critical exponents characterizing a phase transition in quantum error correction.

method: The analysis employs techniques from statistical mechanics, comparing quenched and annealed averages of fidelity in the thermodynamic limit, and utilizing information-theoretic bounds.
model_or_system: The model is a simplified quantum error correction (QEC) scheme involving single-step encoding and decoding using random unitaries and global error channels acting on $N$ qudits.
